payload.title: Nonlinear candidate coverage and visible-prefix selector regret
payload.statement: A legal bank of genuinely different whole-well nonlinear paths can achieve candidate-oracle RMSE below 5, and multi-cut visible-prefix evidence plus calibrated uncertainty can retain enough of that coverage without hidden-label routing.
payload.evidence_for: E010 verifies a 130,252-path legal bank oracle at 4.7510768278 RMSE across 773 wells, proving below-5 candidate coverage. Sixteen families win at least one well.
payload.evidence_against: The best legal selector reaches only 14.7802528528 RMSE, retains about 1.5% of the available oracle gain, regresses spatial group 1 and high-GR-missingness wells, and exceeds the 3 GB memory cap. Family choice explains only 9.5% of the oracle-to-selector gap; coefficient estimation and aggregation explain 90.5%.
payload.next_test: H014/E011: predict low-dimensional path coefficients or control points strictly inside folds, use compact family experts only as secondary structure, preserve E006 fallback, and avoid materializing the full candidate lattice.
